components.name: Primary Button

components.html: About me
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { display:inline-flex; align-items:center; gap:10px; height:52px; padding:0 28px; border:1px solid #14241f; border-radius:999px; background:#14241f; color:#e3eae2; font:500 16px/1 "Newsreader", "Lyon Text", "Iowan Old Style", Georgia, serif; text-decoration:none; transition:background .2s ease, scale .15s ease; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background:#004d26; border-color:#004d26; } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline:2px solid #006633; outline-offset:3px; } .ds-btn-primary:active { scale:.96; }

components.name: Secondary Button
components.description: Quiet companion to the primary: outline pill.
components.css: .ds-btn-secondary { height:52px; padding:0 28px; border:1px solid #c3cfc3; border-radius:999px; background:transparent; color:#14241f; font:500 16px/1 "Newsreader", "Lyon Text", "Iowan Old Style", Georgia, serif; cursor:pointer; transition:border-color .2s ease, scale .15s ease; } .ds-btn-secondary:hover { border-color:#14241f; } .ds-btn-secondary:focus-visible { outline:2px solid #006633; outline-offset:3px; } .ds-btn-secondary:active { scale:.96; }

components.name: Resume Pill
components.description: Header link to the resume; fills with Wimbledon Green on hover and focus.
components.css: .ds-resume { display:inline-flex; align-items:center; height:40px; padding:0 18px; border:1px solid #c3cfc3; border-radius:999px; color:#14241f; font:500 15px/1 "Newsreader", "Lyon Text", "Iowan Old Style", Georgia, serif; text-decoration:none; transition:background .2s ease, color .2s ease, border-color .2s ease, scale .15s ease; } .ds-resume:hover, .ds-resume:focus-visible { background:#006633; border-color:#006633; color:#e3eae2; outline:none; } .ds-resume:active { scale:.96; }

components.name: Step Bar
components.description: Sticky case-study progress: dots on a line that fills green as you read.
components.css: .ds-steps { display:flex; gap:0; margin:0; padding:12px 0 10px; list-style:none; font:400 12px/1.25 "Newsreader", "Lyon Text", "Iowan Old Style", Georgia, serif; color:#4f6159; } .ds-steps li { flex:1; display:grid; justify-items:center; gap:8px; position:relative; } .ds-steps li::before { content:''; position:absolute; top:6px; left:-50%; right:50%; height:2px; background:#c3cfc3; } .ds-steps li:first-child::before { display:none; } .ds-steps li.is-done::before, .ds-steps li.is-now::before { background:#006633; } .ds-steps span { position:relative; width:14px; height:14px; border:2px solid #4f6159; border-radius:50%; background:#e3eae2; box-sizing:border-box; } .ds-steps .is-done span { border-color:#006633; background:#006633; } .ds-steps .is-now span { border-color:#006633; box-shadow:0 0 0 4px #d3e8da; } .ds-steps .is-now { color:#14241f; font-weight:600; }

narrative.overview:
This is a designer-engineer's working notebook kept on sage paper. One serif, Newsreader, does all the talking, from the 60px opening statement down to 13px chips, the way a notebook keeps one hand throughout. The work is shown rather than described: real screens, interactive sandboxes to try, numbered wireframes and honest notes on what was left unfinished. Colour is almost absent. Wimbledon Green appears only where it means something: a reached step, a key phrase, a pressed control.

The pages are calm and generous. A big statement, a lot of air, then evidence. Case studies read like letters: one narrow column of text with pictures, cards and playgrounds stepping wider around it. Dark mode is not inverted chrome but a night lawn, deep green with chalk-white type and a bright Court Mint accent. Motion is scroll-linked and explains the reading order: words light up as you reach them, a journey line draws down to each stop. All of it steps aside for reduced motion and the pause button.
keyCharacteristics: One serif family for every role. Mono appears only for code and data inside sandboxes.
Two themes, both green: Sage Paper by day, Night Lawn by dark.
Flat surfaces. Depth comes from tone and rules, never shadows.
Pills and soft 16px cards that press down slightly when tapped.
Scroll-linked motion that brightens text you can already read and never hides it.

rules.name: The One Green Rule
rules.body: Green is the only hue. It marks meaning (a link, a key phrase, a reached state, focus) and never decorates. Status colours (warn #8a5700, error #b42318) exist for sandboxes and forms only.

rules.name: The Both Lawns Rule
rules.body: Every colour change is made in both themes, and the dark values are defined once for `[data-theme="dark"]` and once for the system preference. Edit both or neither.

rules.name: The Readable Floor Rule
rules.body: Text is never dimmed below AA. Scroll effects rest at 3:1 for large text and 4.5:1 for body text in both themes (see `--sw-floor*` and `--stop-floor` in `carme.css`).

rules.name: The One Hand Rule
rules.body: Newsreader sets every role. A second family appears only when the content itself is code, or is a faithful reproduction of another product's interface.

rules.name: The Measure-in-Em Rule
rules.body: Reading widths are set in em, never px, so a line holds about 75 characters at whatever size the text renders.

rules.name: The Flat Paper Rule
rules.body: Surfaces never float. If something needs separating, give it a tone step or a hairline, not a shadow.

dos: **Do** set every new piece of text in Newsreader, using the hierarchy above.
**Do** make every colour change in both themes, in both dark blocks.
**Do** keep reading text at 32em (case studies) or 31em (ledes).
**Do** use the pill (999px) for anything you can press and 16px for anything that contains.
**Do** give every scroll effect a reduced-motion path that shows the final state, and keep dimmed text at AA.
**Do** reserve space for anything a script inserts after load.
donts: **Don't** add box shadows; use a tone step or a hairline.
**Don't** introduce a second accent hue or use green decoratively.
**Don't** dim text below 3:1 (large) or 4.5:1 (body) at rest, in either theme.
**Don't** add a new font family for site chrome.
